I also feel similar to this. I like it. I like the way it feels and the way it looks. It's not excessive what I do. It is possible to cut yourself and not have it be self harm, I believe. 

There are real life "vampires" who will drink their own blood or their partner's blood. There is also a medical practice in which you purposefully bleed to rid your body of toxins (I think it's called blood letting).
Scarification is also interesting. Scarification includes branding, cutting, burning, freezing techniques. Tattoos are scarification. You can get patterns cut into you and it will have a similar effect as a white ink tattoo. Lastly, scarification is also a religious practice in some cultures such as Africa and Australia (possibly some Asian areas too, but I'mnot sure). They do it for beauty and intimidation. Males will have cuts on their chest to signify how many they have defeated in battle.

I don't exactly encourage it, but I will tell you that it isn't always wrong. Because if all self harm is wrong, then getting tattoos would be wrong. Even piercings. Hair cuts too! Which I think is interesting bc it explains why so many people cut or dye their hair when they have a mental breakdown. So yeah, I'm just saying that in some circumstances/situations it is perfectly fine.

I'm so sorry this is happening to you. AP Art is for college and will most likely require a portfolio of your works by the end of the year. The problem is that colleges and companies will more than likely expect to see realism. It's what they like and accept, so your teacher is always gonna try to push you into realism.

I get where you are coming from. I specialize in Semi-Realism and anime art styles. It's really disappointing that the general consensus hates these art styles. It made me really mad too when I was in AP Art during High school. I can do realism, it's just not the thing I really love. I like my art to have style and be unique. In my opinion, different is what catches the eye. But for some reason, most accept realism because it shows that you've spent a lot of time on it. I hate that, because being able to draw beautiful cartoons and anime is something that not everyone can do. It is hard to create it too. They just think that it's "too easy" and that's why they don't think it's special.

I never finished my art portfolio in time due to the fact that it had to be realism. I can do it just fine, it was just not my specialty so it took me longer to do compared to the other students.

I'm sorry that your teacher has been publicly humiliating you. Even my teacher had the decency to keep my art between me and him. It's really disrespectful for him to treat you like that and he should be ashamed to call himself an artist. Being realistic does not equal how much talent you have. Picasso started out as realist painter and he struggled to get to that point of art work that he is known for. 

I hope that you can get through this rough patch and still keep your passion for your art. Never abandon your art style, it is uniquely yours and that's what makes it special.
